blocking.what_is_wrong: Approval requires complete == true. 21 of 26 plan chunks are unwritten and the e2e suite still covers only the CLI surface, so no behavioural guarantee in DESIGN.md has executable proof yet. This is a sequencing finding, NOT a defect in this iteration's diff: nothing in scan.py or the catalog.py ensure_image narrowing needs to be undone or revisited. scan.py implements all 11 of DESIGN.md section 5.1's scan-time reasons plus section 5.2's two decode-time ones with the rule each is given there, is structurally read-only (os.walk/os.stat/is_symlink/realpath only), prunes rather than descends refused directories, and enforces the benign/abnormal partition at import time so a newly added reason cannot silently inherit benign. FOLLOWUPS F1 is genuinely closed and closed the right way: ensure_image now refreshes only caller-named columns plus last_updated, with status/run_id behind an explicit refresh_state=True (catalog.py:711-716); status and run_id are explicit keyword parameters so they can never arrive through **columns, meaning the refreshed list cannot contain a duplicate assignment and every name in it is present in the INSERT's values dict; first_seen remains write-once. This review confirmed by rg that there is no caller of ensure_image outside catalog.py, so the narrowing broke no call site, and the empirical check is captured in PROGRESS.md:1282 (a done/r1 row survived ensure_image(sha, run_id=r2) unchanged with disposition skip_done, and moved to planned/r2 only with the opt-in, first_seen unchanged).

Gates still entirely unproven by tests: chunk 9 must land E6's full form (a real `classify` over the fixture card proving dominance_ratio decides alone, with no absolute area floor anywhere) plus the second-run-is-a-clean-no-op test that exercises BOTH halves of the idempotency fix -- record_skip's ON CONFLICT(path) upsert and ensure_image's new refresh_state opt-in, where the pipeline must pass refresh_state=True only after plan_disposition returns PROCESS; chunk 11 brings materialize.py with atomic writes and the --link/--hardlink/--dry-run/--reclassify contract; chunk 12's E16 must cover all 13 skip reasons and pin the run's exit class (see note F15: benign skips exit 0, abnormal exit 4); E22 covers fail-loud config; chunks 15-19 bring the species and bird heads, where a low-confidence result must file as `unknown` rather than a guessed species, and where E8 must assert human-readable output directories (chuck_wills_widow, never 022_chuck_will_widow).

notes: Iteration 4 reviewed 49af62f..HEAD: 4fdc624 (scan.py, 392 new lines; catalog.py +25/-4) and bc7d401 (test report). Verdict is CHANGES_REQUESTED for sequencing only; the diff itself is clean and no rework is requested.

The test suite was NOT re-run by this step, per instruction. The verdict rests on the diff plus the captured evidence in docs/test-report.md, with two narrow read-only spot-checks: rg for callers of ensure_image outside catalog.py (none), and rg in docs/design-review.md to confirm the finding number scan.py's docstring cites (line 115, finding 5, titled exactly 'exit code 4 vs 0 for benign skips is self-contradictory, and E2/E16 cannot both pass').

No min_box_area and no absolute box-area floor anywhere in this diff. max_file_bytes is a whole-file st_size cap applied before any decode, which is how DESIGN.md:295 defines it, so it structurally never sees a detection box; section 5.2's pixel cap is the separate reason too_large_pixels, so the catalog cannot confuse a huge file with a huge raster. dominance_ratio remains the only size gate, still guarded executably by the 6 parametrised CLI tests over 10 spellings of an area floor.

Read-only guarantee not violated and slightly strengthened: scan.py has no write call of any kind, and pruning mutates dirnames in place so a refused directory's contents are never even listed. root.resolve() is computed once and is the containment boundary for the symlink_escape check.

I7 fail-loud honoured: scan() raises ConfigError when source_root is None instead of defaulting to the working directory, and walk() raises ConfigError when the root is not a directory (DESIGN section 10.1: fatal, exit 3). No silent substitution introduced.

The import-time partition check (scan.py:103-110) is the most valuable line in the file: a SkipReason added without being classified would inherit 'benign' at the first `not in ABNORMAL_REASONS` test and quietly turn a partial run into exit 0. Failing at import makes that impossible.

os.walk(onerror=...) is correctly supplied: os.walk silently swallows scandir/listdir failures otherwise, so photos inside an unlistable directory would have produced no skipped row at all. The drain sits at the top of the loop body so errors stay in walk order, with a final drain after the loop.

symlink policy matches section 5.1 exactly: symlinked directories are pruned as `symlink` under every flag including --follow-source-symlinks (which governs files only); symlinked files are `symlink` by default and, when followed, still rejected as `symlink_escape` when os.path.realpath is not under the resolved root -- because ingesting it would record a sources.path inside the card for bytes living outside it.

Test hygiene clean: 7 passed / exit 0 with verbatim captured output and a reproducibility re-run, no unit tests, no test outside tests/e2e/, testpaths pinned, nothing deleted or weakened to make the suite green. Identical test set and result to the previous run, which is expected for a chunk that added no test.

F15 (non-blocking) -- the exit class for benign skips deviates from DESIGN.md:1211's literal '4 completed with per-image failures or skips'. scan.py exits 0 when only benign skips happened. This is the right call: docs/design-review.md:115 finding 5 flags that sentence as self-contradictory with E2, and section 10.1's own table marks video/format_disabled/too_large/symlink as 'not an error'/DEBUG. Recorded because the resolution currently lives only in a module docstring -- E2 and E16 must assert the chosen semantics.

F16 (non-blocking) -- _judge_file tests video and raw_not_enabled before unsupported_extension/format_disabled, while section 5.1's table lists them after. Behaviourally right (.mp4 and .cr2 belong to no formats family, so table order would record the less specific unsupported_extension) and both candidates are benign so the exit class is unchanged; only the docstring's claim of 'the fixed precedence order documented there' overstates it.

F17 (non-blocking, self-resolving at chunks 9/12; same shape as F7/F12) -- scan.py has no executable proof at this commit. None of the 13 reasons, the directory pruning, the onerror drain ordering, or exit_code_for is reachable from a --help invocation; correctness rests on this review's reading plus PROGRESS.md's ad-hoc runs.

F18 (non-blocking) -- an unreadable source ROOT surfaces as Skipped(unreadable) (abnormal, exit 4) rather than section 10.1's fatal exit 3 for 'source missing / not a dir / not readable'. walk() checks is_dir() but not readability. It still fails loudly and non-zero, so nothing is silent; add the up-front check in chunk 9 where classify wires the exit codes.

F19 (non-blocking) -- the `while pending_errors: yield pending_errors.pop(0)` drain is duplicated (scan.py:266-268, 281-282) and O(n); a deque or yield-from-then-clear would read better. No behaviour change.

F20 (non-blocking) -- Skipped.benign (property) and module-level is_benign() are two spellings of one predicate and the property has no caller today. is_benign()'s string-accepting form is the load-bearing one: it classifies a reason read back out of the catalog and raises ValueError on an unrecognised value instead of defaulting to benign.
All F15-F20 are appended to docs/FOLLOWUPS.md. None of them withholds approval.
